name: Lisinopril
description: Lisinopril is a medication primarily used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and heart failure. It is also prescribed to improve survival after a heart attack. It works by relaxing blood vessels so that blood can flow more easily.
quickSummary: Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor used to treat high blood pressure and heart failure, and to improve survival after a heart attack. It works by blocking the angiotensin-converting enzyme, which relaxes blood vessels and reduces blood pressure.

uses.description: Managing high blood pressure in adults and children at least 6 years of age.
As an adjunct treatment to help manage symptoms and improve heart function.
Administered within 24 hours of a heart attack to improve hemodynamic stability and survival rates.

sideEffects.title: Dry Cough
sideEffects.description: The most common side effect of ACE inhibitors. Usually subsides upon discontinuation.

sideEffects.title: Dizziness
sideEffects.description: Particularly when standing up quickly. Occurs due to blood pressure changes.

sideEffects.title: Headache
sideEffects.description: Mild to moderate tension-style headaches reported in 5% of patients.

sideEffects.title: Fatigue
sideEffects.description: General feeling of low energy as the body adjusts to lower blood pressure.

interactions.description: Lisinopril can increase potassium levels. Combining with supplements or potassium-sparing diuretics may lead to hyperkalemia.
Drugs like ibuprofen or naproxen can reduce the blood pressure lowering effect of lisinopril and may increase the risk of kidney issues.
Lisinopril may increase the amount of lithium in your blood, potentially leading to lithium toxicity.

warnings.title: Fetal Toxicity
warnings.description: Black Box Warning: When pregnancy is detected, discontinue lisinopril as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.

warnings.title: Angioedema
warnings.description: Seek immediate medical attention if you experience swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, as this can obstruct breathing.
